ShortDescription.Value: Real timetables for public transport — fixed departures, auto-sized fleets and terminus timing points. Works for buses, trams, trains, metros, ferries and planes.

Publish.LongDescription:
Turn any public-transport line into a scheduled service. Works for every passenger type: buses, trams, trains, metros, ferries and aircraft.
WHAT'S NEW IN 0.5.3:
- The realism checkboxes from before 0.5 are back on the Options page, including the one a lot of you were using: let the mod manage vehicle counts, but size them from the game's own estimate instead of the measured loop. High-frequency lines no longer have to be provisioned for their full real loop to be managed. - Both realism settings start off. If you had them on before 0.5 they come back on by themselves. If you started during 0.5.x your vehicle counts will fall, and switching "Provision fleet for real travel time" back on restores them. - A one-time notice explains this when you load a city with timetables, and can switch both on for you. - Posted stop times and vehicle counts are now worked out from the same measurement. - Three settings that had only ever been in English are now translated into all 11 languages.
Earlier in 0.5.2.2:
- Select a vehicle to see where it stands against the schedule and when it is due at its next stop. A vehicle held at a stop says it is waiting for its departure rather than reporting it as a delay.
Earlier in 0.5.1:
- Vehicle counts stop over-shooting. The mod times how long a line really takes to go round, and on a busy line it could mistake two loops for one and then average that mistake in permanently. It now takes the middle reading rather than the average, so a stray bad timing no longer drags the answer up. - Lines stop suddenly asking for far more vehicles for no visible reason. A safety net meant for edited routes was firing on healthy lines and throwing away everything they had learned. It now keeps the learning and simply recalibrates. - The TIMETABLE panel no longer appears twice after loading a second city without restarting the game.
Earlier in 0.5.0:
- Your settings are saved properly now. All of my mods shared one internal name for their settings, and the game resolves them by that name, so all but one wrote nowhere and anything you changed came back as default the next session. - Vehicle counts are now a single setting with two states: the mod sizes your fleets, or you do. - Realistic travel time is no longer optional. It is always on, it costs nothing, and it is the point of the mod. - Fleet growth is staggered. Extra vehicles used to leave the depot together and enter the line as one clump, which is the bunching this mod exists to prevent. They now arrive one per departure interval. - Vehicles no longer throw off passengers who are already boarding, and "Maximum stop time" caps how long they will wait for them. - Missed departures are caught up, measured travel times survive quitting, and there is a one-click clean uninstall.
Full detail in the changelog.
Per line you opt in and set:
- a first departure time and peak / off-peak / night intervals (the global peak windows are configurable), - OR give a line its OWN peak hours: any line can override the global rush with two custom windows and its own peak interval, so a line serving a factory shift, a school run or a stadium can run its own rush hour while the rest of the network keeps to the city-wide one, - the mod then DERIVES how many vehicles the line needs to hold that headway and sizes the line to it, without touching the vehicle-count slider on any other line, - a terminus stop (timing point) where early vehicles are held to the scheduled departure, and where surplus vehicles retire — after finishing their loop and dropping passengers, not mid-route.
Select any stop to open a printed-timetable departure board for every line that serves it, listed from the first departure of the day. Day-only and night-only lines only show and run the intervals that apply to them, and a night line is scheduled inside the night window.
No timetable set = the line runs exactly like vanilla. Everything is controlled from the line's own info panel plus a floating departures board.
Posted times come from each line's REAL measured loop, not the game's estimate. The game's estimate is optimistic — it ignores the time vehicles lose braking, accelerating and loading passengers at every stop, and real loops measure up to 3x it — so times based on it drift ahead of reality. The mod measures each line as it runs and saves the result with your city, so posted times are right from the moment you load rather than after a day or two of learning. This used to be an optional setting; it is now simply how the mod works.
SETTINGS (a plain timetable needs none of them):
- "Vehicle counts": either the mod sizes each line's fleet to hold the headway you set, or you keep control. Because it sizes to the REAL measured loop, a stop-dense line needs roughly twice the vehicles the game's own estimate would suggest, so expect more vehicles than vanilla runs. Switch it to "I manage them" to hand every count back, whether you prefer the game's "Assigned Vehicles" slider or a dedicated fleet mod. - "Stop at every stop (even empty ones)" (free, off by default): by default a bus skips a stop where nobody boards or alights, so that stop isn't held to schedule; the terminus is now always honoured, and this extends that to every stop. Lines run a little slower. - "Maximum stop time" for buses and for rail (3 minutes each by default): how long a vehicle may keep waiting PAST its posted departure for passengers who are already boarding. It is a limit, not a target — a vehicle with nobody boarding still leaves exactly on its posted minute, and this setting never delays it by a second. Raise the rail value if you see people piling up on a busy platform: a train or metro exchanging a full platform takes far longer to load, and unlike a bus it can never skip a stop. Set it to 0 to leave on the dot and wait for nobody. - "Realistic Trips / slow-time compatibility" (ALPHA, off by default): keeps timing correct if you run a mod that lengthens the in-game day (Time2Work / Realistic Trips). Leave off otherwise.
CLEAN UNINSTALL: Options has a "Remove all mod data from this save" button. It reverts every line to the base game and deletes the mod's data from your city, so you can uninstall with nothing left behind. It clears your timetables, so it asks first — and after confirming, let the game run for a moment before you save.
Recommended: leave everything at its defaults. Raise "Maximum stop time" for rail if you see passengers piling up on a busy platform, and switch "Vehicle counts" to "I manage them" if you would rather own your fleet sizes yourself.
KNOWN ISSUES:
- "Vehicles no longer un-bunch after removing the mod." The mod writes two values into a line's save data — an "unbunching factor" (an early pre-v0.2.3 build), and a "vehicle interval" it uses to size the fleet. If you remove or disable the mod WITHOUT first switching a line's timetable off, those values can stay frozen in the save (the base game never resets them), so vehicles leave a stop immediately without spacing out. FIXED as of v0.3.2.2: the mod now repairs both automatically on load, for every line, and safely — the vehicle interval is rebuilt from the line's own settings, so a count you set by hand with "Assigned Vehicles" is preserved. To repair an affected save: subscribe to v0.3.2.2 (or newer), load your city, then save. Normal unbunching returns, and you can keep or remove the mod afterwards.
CREDITS: per-line custom peak windows (each line can override the global peak hours and run its own peak interval) were contributed by incconutwo. The per-vehicle schedule readout was suggested by ThisGuySucksAtCitys. Thank you both. Community bug reports have driven several releases, including the terminus stop fix, the mid-route spawn fix and the missed-trip catch-up.
Source (open source, MIT): https://github.com/AmicusDeus/TransitTimetables
Localized into 11 languages (German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese-BR, Russian, Chinese Simplified & Traditional). Translations are machine-generated — corrections welcome.
Made with Claude Code's Opus 4.8 and Fable 5 models.
Publish.ChangeLog:
v0.5.3 [BETA] - The realism toggles are back
- The checkboxes from before 0.5 are on the Options page again: "Manage vehicle count", "Provision fleet for real travel time" and "Realistic travel time". 0.5 folded them into one dropdown, and doing so removed the middle option: let the mod manage vehicle counts, but size them from the game's own estimate rather than the measured loop. That combination is back, so a high-frequency line can be managed without being provisioned for its full real loop.
- Both realism settings start OFF. If you had them switched on before 0.5, that choice is still in your settings file and comes back by itself, so nothing changes for you. If you started using the mod during 0.5.x, where they were always on, your lines will size from the estimate again and your vehicle counts WILL FALL. Switch "Provision fleet for real travel time" back on to keep the 0.5.x behaviour.
- A one-time notice explains this the first time you load a city that has timetables, and can switch both settings on for you. Dismissing it leaves your city exactly as it is.
- FIX: posted stop times and vehicle counts are now worked out from the same measurement. v0.5.1 stopped vehicle counts being thrown off by a mistimed lap, but the posted times were still using the old averaging, so a line could be sized from one figure and timetabled from another.
- Three settings that had only ever appeared in English, including the two stop-time limits, are now translated into all 11 supported languages, along with everything added in 0.5.2.
v0.5.2.2 [BETA] - See how late a vehicle is running
- NEW: select a bus, tram or train on a timetabled line and its info panel tells you where it stands against the schedule. At a stop it says when it departs, and if it is waiting there early it says so plainly rather than calling it a delay, because holding an early vehicle until its departure time is the whole point of a timetable. On the move it gives the next stop's due time, and only claims the vehicle is behind once that time has passed and it still has not arrived. (Requested by ThisGuySucksAtCitys - thank you.)
- A vehicle that joined its line partway round, which is what happens when one leaves a depot, says it is not yet on the timetable. It has no scheduled departure to be measured against until it first reaches the terminus, so there is nothing honest to report before then.
- While a line is still learning how long its route really takes, the panel says so, since those times will still move.
v0.5.1 [BETA] - Vehicle counts stop over-shooting, and stop jumping on their own
- FIX: some lines asked for far too many vehicles. The mod times how long a line takes to go round by watching a vehicle leave the terminus and come back, and on a busy line it could miss a return and record two loops as one. It used to average every reading together, so those doubled timings dragged the answer up permanently. It now takes the middle reading instead, so a stray bad timing no longer moves it.
- FIX: a line could suddenly demand a lot more vehicles for no visible reason. A safety net meant for edited routes was firing on healthy lines and discarding everything they had learned, sometimes hundreds of timed laps, then restarting from whichever odd reading had triggered it. It now keeps what it has learned and simply recalibrates.
- FIX: the TIMETABLE panel appeared twice on a line if you returned to the main menu and loaded another city without restarting the game.
- The line panel now says whether a line is still measuring, refining, or measured, and warns while refining that its vehicle count is cautious and may rise.
